item.content:encoded: Negotiators for the US, Ukraine and Europeans held six hours of talks in Miami on Friday with the aim of reaching agreement on a unified proposal to end the war in Ukraine, a person familiar with the talks said. The goal is to reach agreement on such a proposal in the coming weeks so it can be presented to Russia in order to seek a breakthrough before the winter, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The talks came on the same day that US President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"supply diesel to global markets"] in an effort to lower fuel prices, while his administration lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for the war. The deal was criticized by US lawmakers and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. "All that money goes toward the war against people, against Ukraine, against all of us. I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair," Zelenskiy said in a statement. Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Trump that an immediate [USN:L1N45V0ZL TEXT:"resumption of peace talks was unlikely"], citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow. The talks in Miami included US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and delegations from Ukraine as well as representatives from Europe and NATO. The negotiators covered a lengthy list of topics in the discussions, including a post-war package for Ukraine that would include security guarantees from the US and from Europe, the person said. Also discussed were a post-war economic plan for Ukraine and a pathway to accession to the European Union for Kyiv, the person said. In a sensitive subject, the delegations discussed "some ideas" on territory, the person said, declining to elaborate. Ukraine has been adamant that Russia cede territory it has seized during the conflict. President Donald Trump has said both sides will need to compromise. The person said the delegations also discussed a Europe-Russia security architecture that would set the stage for peaceful years ahead. The person did not provide details.

item.title: Trump leva à Suprema Corte dos EUA ação contra Hillary Clinton relativa à eleição de 2016
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, solicitou nesta sexta-feira à Suprema Corte que restabelecesse sua ação judicial indeferida contra sua rival democrata nas eleições de 2016, Hillary Clinton, na qual a acusava de conspirar com o ex-diretor do FBI James Comey e outros para manipular a eleição daquele ano, associando sua campanha à Rússia.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, solicitou nesta sexta-feira à Suprema Corte que restabelecesse sua ação judicial indeferida contra sua rival democrata nas eleições de 2016, Hillary Clinton, na qual a acusava de conspirar com o ex-diretor do FBI James Comey e outros para manipular a eleição daquele ano, associando sua campanha à Rússia. O presidente republicano entrou com o recurso depois que um juiz federal indeferiu o processo e impôs quase US$1 milhão em sanções contra Trump e uma de suas advogadas por terem movido uma ação “frívola”. Posteriormente, um tribunal de apelação dos EUA manteve o indeferimento e as sanções. Em 2022, quando já não ocupava o cargo após perder a eleição de 2020, Trump processou Hillary, Comey, o ex-oficial da inteligência britânica Christopher Steele, o Comitê Nacional Democrata e vários outros em uma longa ação movida no tribunal federal da Flórida. Trump, que tem um histórico de processar adversários, alegou que, na corrida para a eleição de 2016, Hillary conspirou com aliados para desacreditá-lo por meio de uma “narrativa falsa” de que ele e sua campanha teriam agido em conluio com a Rússia. A longa ação alegava “criminalidade organizada” e uma “conspiração para cometer falsidade prejudicial”, entre outras alegações. Trump derrotou Hillary naquela eleição, apesar de ter perdido o voto popular nacional, e cumpriu seu primeiro mandato de 2017 a 2021. Autoridades do governo dos EUA acusaram a Rússia de interferir na eleição de 2016, e uma investigação liderada pelo ex-chefe do FBI Robert Mueller documentou contatos extensos entre a campanha de Trump e agentes russos que buscavam influenciar a eleição a seu favor. Trump chamou a ideia de interferência russa de “farsa”. Desde que perdeu para o democrata Joe Biden em 2020, Trump tem feito alegações falsas de fraude eleitoral generalizada na eleição daquele ano. Trump reconquistou a Presidência ao derrotar a democrata Kamala Harris em 2024 e continua a fazer essas alegações falsas. O juiz federal Donald Middlebrooks indeferiu a ação movida por Trump contra Clinton, citando inúmeras falhas, incluindo o fato de Trump ter esperado tempo demais para apresentar algumas das alegações. O juiz comparou a ação de Trump a um “manifesto político de duzentas páginas que expõe suas queixas contra aqueles que se opuseram a ele”. Middlebrooks posteriormente ordenou que Trump e sua principal advogada no caso, Alina Habba, pagassem quase US$1 milhão em honorários e custas, impondo as sanções por terem movido uma ação que, segundo o juiz, tinha como objetivo “promover de forma desonesta uma narrativa política”. O juiz também repreendeu Trump e seus advogados por um “padrão contínuo de uso indevido dos tribunais”. Middlebrooks concluiu que a ação utilizou táticas processuais abusivas, continha alegações factuais “conscientemente falsas” e invocava teorias jurídicas “frívolas”. O Tribunal Federal de Apelações do 11º Circuito, com sede em Atlanta, manteve as decisões do juiz em 2025, incluindo as sanções.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has authorized Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) , to operate in the Latin American country. The authorization is part of an agreement with the US firm, the Venezuelan government said in a statement on Friday. The company's satellite-internet unit has continued to expand its global subscriber base, aided by launches of additional satellites and a growing range of consumer, enterprise, aviation, maritime and government services.

item.title: David Puig leaves LIV as Bryson DeChambeau reportedly eyes Europe starts
item.description: The DP World Tour, formerly known as the European Tour, may hold the key for many players departing LIV Golf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The DP World Tour, formerly known as the European Tour, may hold the key for many players departing LIV Golf. Spanish youngster David Puig announced Thursday that he would not stay with LIV as it restructures for the future, switching his membership to the DP World Tour. And two-time major champion Bryson DeChambeau is reportedly weighing more starts in Europe, as well. "I don't see myself playing in the LIV 2.0," Puig told reporters at the Spanish Open, a DP World Tour event. "It's a decision I've made. I hope to play the European Tour next year, which I really enjoy, with a fuller schedule." Puig, 24, was a strong amateur golfer and starred collegiately at Arizona State. He played in two LIV events while still an amateur in 2022, when the league was still in its infancy, and signed with LIV once he turned pro. While Puig never won an individual tournament title in his four-plus years with LIV, he maintained eligibility for some DP World Tour and Asian Tour events and earned the biggest win of his career last November at the Australian PGA Championship. In pursuing full-time DP World Tour membership, Puig follows Spanish stars Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia from LIV back to Europe. Puig played for Garcia's Fireballs GC while with the team-based league. Garcia was granted release from his LIV contract earlier this week. DeChambeau and Rahm, meanwhile, are among the small number of elite players whose decisions will make or break the so-called LIV 2.0 plan. Rahm made his decision known earlier this week that he would leave LIV, and golf insider Alan Shipnuck reported late last month that DeChambeau was still going back and forth on his final decision. The Telegraph reported that DeChambeau's team has contacted DP World Tour brass about which tournaments he could appear at in 2027. The report made clear that DeChambeau is not pursuing membership on the European tour, the way Patrick Reed did when he left LIV at the start of 2026, a path Rahm will now emulate. LIV members have until Oct. 25 to commit to playing for the league next year. LIV still needs commitments from a sufficient number of players with outstanding financial claims against the league to satisfy the terms set by its restructuring partner, BC Partners Credit. --Field Level Media

item.title: UAW President Shawn Fain declares victory in race for second term
item.description: United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain declared victory on Friday in a race to maintain his position as head of the 400,000-member union.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall
item.content:encoded: United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain declared victory on Friday in a race to maintain his position as head of the 400,000-member union. Fain, 57, who rose to national prominence during a 2023 strike against General Motors (GM.N) , Ford (F.N) and Chrysler-parent Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , received a majority of the votes and easily topped five challengers, according to preliminary ballot totals released by a federal monitor overseeing the vote. Fain had widely been expected to win the balloting, which the Detroit Three automakers were watching closely as they look ahead to 2028 contract negotiations. The companies are wary of raising their labor costs at a time when the auto industry is grappling with weaker vehicle demand and intensifying competition. “One thing I know about our membership is they're ready to fight,” Fain said in an interview with Reuters. “They know they deserve better. And let's not fool ourselves. All these companies are massively profitable.” Fain has pointed to the next round of negotiations as an opportunity to secure gains beyond the union's landmark 2023 contract, which delivered wage increases of more than 25% over the four-year life of the agreement. The UAW is already urging members to strike in the spring of 2028, when current contracts with the Detroit automakers expire. GM, Ford and Stellantis did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Fain's declared victory late Friday. FAIN’S COMBATIVE APPROACH LED TO GAINS In 2023, just months after narrowly winning his seat, Fain took an unorthodox, combative stance against the automakers. He insisted on bargaining with all three automakers at once, a departure from past practice, in which the union got an agreement at one company to use as a template for the other two. Eventually, he launched simultaneous strikes at factories across all three automakers, a first for the union. “Shawn Fain will continue to take an aggressive approach to collective bargaining. The challenge this time will be that the companies will be well aware” of that approach, said Stephen Silvia, a labor expert from American University. DETROIT AUTOMAKERS LEERY OF LABOR-COST INCREASES Fain said on Friday that in 2028 he plans to push to restore pensions for all workers, a benefit that ended for new hires in 2007, around the time of the near-collapse of domestic US auto companies. GM, Ford and Stellantis, meanwhile, have been stung by tariff expenses, higher raw-materials costs and an expensive rollback of their electric-vehicle plans amid weak US demand. Executives are likely to push back against any meaningful labor-cost increases, said Marick Masters, business professor emeritus at Detroit’s Wayne State University. “The recipe is there for a major confrontation with the companies being in a less favorable position to withstand the pressures,” he said.

item.title: Ukraine-Poutine minimise une reprise immédiate des discussions, dit le Kremlin
item.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a dit vendredi à son homologue américain Donald Trump que Kyiv avait sapé la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate des négociations de paix trilatérales après avoir mené des frappes de drones à Moscou durant les élections législatives qui se sont déroulées le mois dernier, a fait savoir le Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a dit vendredi à son homologue américain Donald Trump que Kyiv avait sapé la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate des négociations de paix trilatérales après avoir mené des frappes de drones à Moscou durant les élections législatives qui se sont déroulées le mois dernier, a fait savoir le Kremlin. Vladimir Poutine avait dit que Moscou était prêt à reprendre les négociations avec Kyiv après la tenue des élections législatives. L'Ukraine a toutefois lancé des attaques contre la capitale russe et a frappé des bureaux de vote, ce qui, selon le chef du Kremlin, a mis en péril le processus de paix. "En lançant le jour le plus important des élections une attaque de drones à grande échelle contre Moscou, d'autres villes et des bureaux de votes, et en prenant pour cible certaines personnes impliquées dans l'organisation des élections, le régime de Kyiv a, en réalité, interrompu la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate du processus de négociation", a déclaré le conseiller du Kremlin Iouri Ouchakov. "Comme le président l'a dit, nous allons désormais évaluer quand ces négociations pourront reprendre", a-t-il ajouté au sujet des discussions trilatérales entre la Russie, les Etats-Unis et l'Ukraine. Iouri Ouchakov a indiqué que, durant leur appel, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump avaient abordé d'importantes initiatives économiques, notamment de potentielles livraisons de carburant russe. Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi qu'à l'issue d'une discussion "très fructueuse" qu'il avait eue avec Vladimir Poutine, la Russie avait accepté de livrer immédiatement plus de 300.000 tonnes de [USN:L8N45V1O6 TEXT:"diesel"] sur les marchés américain et mondial.

item.title: Alcolumbre pauta para 4ª-feira votação da PEC do fim da jornada 6x1
item.description: O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), pautou a votação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal para a próxima quarta-feira, quando ocorre a quinta sessão de discussão da matéria.
item.dc:creator: Maria Marcello
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), pautou a votação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal para a próxima quarta-feira, quando ocorre a quinta sessão de discussão da matéria. Pelas regras regimentais, qualquer PEC precisa passar por cinco sessões de discussão para então ser votada em primeiro turno -- o Senado já realizou três dessas sessões nesta semana, e tem mais duas previstas para a próxima, na terça e na quarta-feira. "Pautei para quarta-feira (14) a votação, em primeiro turno, da PEC 221, de 2019, que trata do fim da escala 6x1", disse o presidente do Senado em nota distribuída por sua assessoria. "Cumpro, assim, o compromisso de colocar a proposta em votação, com responsabilidade, diálogo e respeito ao rito regimental. Caberá a cada senador e a cada senadora decidir com liberdade, consciência e convicção", acrescentou o senador. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que concorre à reeleição, é favorável à PEC e tem usado a defesa de sua aprovação como plataforma de campanha. Lula chegou a desafiar o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) -- que venceu o primeiro turno da disputa presidencial no domingo e enfrenta Lula no dia 25 de outubro --, e seu partido a votarem favoravelmente à proposta. Flávio, que se opõe à PEC, acusa Lula de estar sendo oportunista. O senador e seus aliados têm defendido em declarações públicas uma proposta alternativa que leve em conta uma jornada flexível e a remuneração proporcional à hora trabalhada, defendendo a prevalência de acordos individuais entre empregados e patrões sobre convenções coletivas. Caso seja aprovada em primeiro turno, com no mínimo 49 votos, a PEC precisa ser discutida por mais três sessões, para então ser votada em segundo turno. Segundo a Agência Senado, a líder do governo no Senado, senadora Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), está coletando assinaturas para um requerimento que possa acelerar o calendário de votação da PEC, de forma a ter sua tramitação concluída na Casa na penúltima semana de outubro, antes do segundo turno da eleição presidencial. A PEC em discussão no Senado prevê que a jornada de trabalho terá uma redução de 2 horas semanais das 44 atuais já nos 60 dias depois que a proposta for promulgada. A carga horária sofrerá um decréscimo de mais 2 horas um ano após a primeira redução. A proposta também estabelece o piso de duas folgas semanais, uma delas preferencialmente no domingo, e garante que não haverá redução de salário.

item.title: Trump takes suit against Hillary Clinton over 2016 election to Supreme Court
item.description: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia. The Republican president filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly $1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A US appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions. Trump's lawyers wrote in the appeal that Supreme Court review of the case is needed in order to protect the presidency. They wrote that the decisions by the lower courts reflect "a deeply troubling trend of federal courts using sanctions and disciplinary threats to punish the president and his lawyers for legitimate legal positions that those courts (erroneously) reject." In 2022, when he was out of office after losing the 2020 election, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida. Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia. The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood," among other claims. Trump defeated Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021. US government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between members of the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favor. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax." Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Trump regained the presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024, and has continued to make those false claims. 'POLITICAL MANIFESTO' US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks [USN:L1N30G0Q8 TEXT:"dismissed"] Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him." Middlebrooks later ordered Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly $1 million in fees and costs, imposing the [USN:L1N345068 TEXT:"sanctions"] for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative." The judge also faulted Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts." Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories. The Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions. "Many of Trump's and Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated. In Friday's filing, lawyers for Trump and Habba said the time limit for filing the lawsuit should have been extended because he chose to defer suing during his first term in office in order to carry out his constitutional responsibilities as president. "This court's intervention is necessary to protect the presidency, and to prevent judicial disagreement from becoming a license to punish its advocates," the filing stated. Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the Justice Department, issued a [USN:KCN1RU2MF TEXT:"2019 report"] on his investigation. The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion," but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities." Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the election in Trump's favor. Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to look into potential missteps by the FBI. In a [USN:L1N37C2MA TEXT:"2023 report"], Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe. Trump's Justice Department last year indicted Comey, one of several adversaries of the president hit with criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorizing leaks to the news media. A federal judge subsequently [USN:S0N3U5043 TEXT:"dismissed the indictment"], finding that the prosecutor who Trump handpicked to prosecute Comey had been unlawfully appointed. Steele, working for an opposition research firm that was hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier that alleged ties between Trump's campaign and Russia as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Trump denied.

item.title: Em conversa telefônica com Trump, Putin minimizou chance de retomada imediata das negociações com Ucrânia, diz Kremlin
item.description: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, nesta sexta-feira, que Kiev havia prejudicado a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata das negociações trilaterais de paz na Ucrânia depois de ter atacado Moscou com drones durante as eleições do mês passado, informou o Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, nesta sexta-feira, que Kiev havia prejudicado a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata das negociações trilaterais de paz na Ucrânia depois de ter atacado Moscou com drones durante as eleições do mês passado, informou o Kremlin. Trump tem tentado, até o momento sem sucesso, intermediar um acordo de paz para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia, que teve início com a invasão russa em fevereiro de 2022. O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, afirmou na quinta-feira que a guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia está em um impasse perigoso e que os Estados Unidos continuarão trabalhando em busca de um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito. Putin havia afirmado que Moscou estava pronta para retomar as negociações com Kiev após as eleições parlamentares russas do mês passado, mas a Ucrânia lançou ataques contra Moscou e atingiu seções eleitorais, colocando o processo de paz em risco, segundo ele. “Ao lançar um ataque maciço com drones contra Moscou, outras cidades e seções eleitorais, bem como contra indivíduos específicos envolvidos na organização da eleição, no dia principal da votação, o regime de Kiev efetivamente inviabilizou a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata do processo de negociação”, disse o assessor de política externa do Kremlin, Yuri Ushakov, sobre a ligação com Trump. “E agora, como disse o presidente, vamos avaliar quando essas negociações poderão ser retomadas”, acrescentou ele, referindo-se às negociações trilaterais envolvendo os EUA, a Rússia e a Ucrânia. Ushakov também disse que Putin e Trump discutiram importantes iniciativas econômicas durante a ligação, incluindo possíveis fornecimentos de combustível russo. Trump havia dito mais cedo, após a ligação com Putin, que a Rússia havia concordado em fornecer diesel imediatamente aos mercados dos EUA e globais, em um esforço para reduzir os preços dos combustíveis antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA no mês que vem, embora analistas tenham afirmado que as quantidades provavelmente não reduziriam os preços de forma significativa.

item.title: Queen Camilla on the joy of reading despite king's laughter and her tears
item.description: Britain's Queen Camilla and King Charles spend their evenings reading before dinner, a quiet time which is interrupted by either his laughter or her tears, she told a documentary aimed at reversing the decline in reading for enjoyment in the UK.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Queen Camilla and King Charles spend their evenings reading before dinner, a quiet time which is interrupted by either his laughter or her tears, she told a documentary aimed at reversing the decline in reading for enjoyment in the UK. "When I'm deep in a book, I'll hear him roaring with laughter about something. It's very off-putting," she said, giving a rare glimpse of their private life at Clarence House. "Or I'll suddenly start weeping." Camilla, 79, has been a keen reader her whole life. After the success of a pandemic-era book club she set up on social media, she launched a charity to promote the benefits of reading three years ago. In Britain, the percentage of children and young people who enjoy books hit its lowest level in 20 years last year, according to the National Literacy Trust, which is now working with the government and Camilla's charity to try to turn this around. "I left school quite young, so reading has been most of my education. You learn so much about people, about life," Camilla told the documentary, "The Book That Changed My Life", which will air on the BBC on Wednesday. When Charles laughs out loud, Camilla knows he will be reading a book by "Jeeves and Wooster" creator P.G. Wodehouse. She said he also loved biographies, while she likes historical fiction and thrillers. She said books helped her father survive more than two years as a prisoner of war in Germany in the early 1940s, an experience he then wrote a book about. "You're not thinking of yourself when you're reading, you can immerse yourself into other people's lives and that does relieve the stress," she said. Charles is still receiving treatment for [USN:L8N44G0CW TEXT:"cancer"] and managing the fallout from [USN:L8N3Z81KN TEXT:"the arrest"] of his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who denies wrongdoing, as well as negotiating the relationship with his younger son, [USN:L8N4590QP TEXT:"Prince Harry"], who has returned from the US to live in Britain. Meanwhile, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", a memoir by Charles Spencer, the brother of Charles' first wife, has become a bestseller. Buckingham Palace rejected in [USN:L8N4581JE TEXT:"unusually strong terms"] the book's version of conversations surrounding Diana's death in 1997.

item.title: Colombia firma nueve contratos mineros con inversiones proyectadas de 16,8 millones de dólares
item.description: Colombia firmó nueve contratos especiales de exploración y explotación de minerales estratégicos, como cobre, oro y fosfatos, con los que proyecta inversiones cercanas a 54.000 millones de pesos (16,8 millones de dólares), informó el viernes la Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombia firmó nueve contratos especiales de exploración y explotación de minerales estratégicos, como cobre, oro y fosfatos, con los que proyecta inversiones cercanas a 54.000 millones de pesos (16,8 millones de dólares), informó el viernes la Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM). Los contratos se firmaron dentro de las Rondas Mineras 2026 y corresponden a Áreas Estratégicas Mineras en los departamentos de Cesar, La Guajira, Antioquia, Tolima y Huila, precisó un comunicado de la entidad. Ocho contratos son de la ronda de cobre, oro y polimetálicos, y uno es de la ronda de fosfatos. Entre las empresas que recibieron los contratos se encuentran la china Zijin Mining y OP Gold Capital, informó la ANM. Este modelo de contratación busca dar más seguridad jurídica a los inversionistas y reducir los riesgos, los conflictos y los tiempos de desarrollo de los proyectos, de acuerdo con la ANM. "Sigamos haciendo estos esfuerzos de generar más minería, más desarrollo, más riqueza, mejor economía, mejor educación para todas las regiones de Colombia", dijo el presidente de la ANM, Juan Camilo Valencia, citado en el comunicado. Al mismo tiempo, la agencia firmó 44 nuevas titulaciones mineras en 14 departamentos. Antioquia tiene el mayor número, con 10 títulos, seguida de Huila con nueve, Chocó con seis y Norte de Santander con cinco. Entre esos títulos hay 19 contratos de concesión: 11 de mediana minería y ocho de pequeña minería, que cubren minerales metálicos, materiales de construcción, minerales industriales y carbón. (1 dólar = 3.218,75 pesos)

item.title: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a $2.5 billion valuation, sources say
item.description: Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.
item.dc:creator: Max Cherney, Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising. Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents. The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change. Intel (INTC.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) , which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market. Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones. The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said. Nuvacore declined to comment. The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple (AAPL.O) executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm (QCOM.O) for [USN:KBN29I1OO TEXT:"$1.4 billion in 2021"]. Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned. Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand. Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data. Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts. Shares in both companies have risen more than 180% this year. Nvidia (NVDA.O) launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to [USN:L4N41V0P1 TEXT:"sell $20 billion worth"] of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

item.title: Christian-conservative wireless provider Patriot Mobile files for US IPO
item.description: Patriot Mobile disclosed a 21% increase in first-half revenue in its paperwork for a US initial public offering on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Patriot Mobile disclosed a 21% increase in first-half revenue in its paperwork for a US initial public offering on Friday. Revenue rose to $53.4 million in the six months ended June 30, from $44 million a year earlier. Net loss widened to $4.6 million from $1.8 million during the period Patriot Mobile is a Christian-conservative mobile virtual network operator based in Texas The company was a major sponsor of the 2026 Republican National Committee Midterm Convention in Dallas, where Vice President JD Vance and other administration officials spoke Founded in 2013 as a niche cellular reseller, Patriot Mobile officially dropped its traditional startup imagery in 2016 and rebranded aggressively to lean into conservative activism The company plans to use the proceeds from the offering to repay debt and for general corporate purposes, including working capital, expansion and potential acquisitions It plans to list its shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "PTRT". Northland Securities is the sole book-running manager of the offering

item.title: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
item.description: A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, a federal court filing showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Freifeld, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia (NVDA.O) AI chips to China, a federal court filing showed on Friday. Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracies to violate US export controls, smuggle goods from the US, defraud the country and obstruct justice. He entered the plea on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan. The United States and China are competing for dominance in AI, with both investing billions of dollars in a technology seen as critical to economic growth, national security and military capabilities. In March, [USN:L1N4071M5 TEXT:"prosecutors charged"] Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server maker, with conspiring to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. The scheme began around October 2023, with Sun and others conspiring to export servers from a US manufacturer, widely believed to be Super Micro, to China without the required licenses, according to the indictment. Asked for comment on the guilty plea, California-based Super Micro referred to its prior statements that the company was not named as a defendant in the indictment and that it had no impact on its business operations. [USN:L4N40Q1GS TEXT:"Super Micro"] terminated Sun and cut ties with the other defendants earlier this year. A lawyer for Sun declined to comment. Also indicted were the co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and Ruei-Tsang "Steven" Chang, who was a sales manager at Super Micro's Taiwan office, while Sun was a contractor. A lawyer for Liaw - who co-founded Super Micro in 1993 and joined its board in 2023 - did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Chang's lawyer could not immediately be reached for comment. The indictment described Sun as a broker and “fixer” who facilitated orders and took steps to conceal the scheme. He helped stage "dummy" servers in December 2025 and made false statements to a US Department of Commerce officer during an inspection of supposedly stored servers, which had already been diverted to China, according to the indictment. Washington has restricted sales of advanced AI chips to China, citing national security concerns. The indictment said Nvidia's B200, H100 and H200 graphics processing units, and servers containing them, were subject to the restrictions.

item.title: ATUALIZA 1 CSN negocia com grupo espanhol venda da SWT por 550 mi de euros
item.description: A CSN anunciou nesta sexta-feira assinatura de acordo vinculante para venda de sua usina de aços longos na Alemanha, atribuindo um valor para o negócio de 550 milhões de euros, segundo fato relevante.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A CSN (CSNA3.SA) anunciou nesta sexta-feira assinatura de acordo vinculante para venda de sua usina de aços longos na Alemanha, atribuindo um valor para o negócio de 550 milhões de euros, segundo fato relevante. A companhia, que está tentando reduzir endividamento, afirmou que o termo vinculante foi assinado pela espanhola Bipadosa, controladora do grupo siderúrgico espanhol Megasa. O período de exclusividade para assinatura de documentos definitivos para a conclusão do negócio é de 10 semanas, afirmou a CSN. A SWT foi comprada pela CSN em 2012. Na época o valor anunciado pela companhia brasileira para o negócio foi de 482,5 milhões de euros. "considerando a premissa de endividamento zero". A usina alemã tem capacidade instalada de 1,1 milhão de toneladas de aços longos por ano. "A potencial alienação das ações da SWT representa mais um passo importante no programa de desinvestimentos da CSN com o propósito de reduzir o seu atual nível de endividamento", afirmou a CSN no fato relevante. Nos resultados de segundo trimestre deste ano, a CSN afirmou que a SWT havia atingido sua melhor marca de vendas desde o primeiro trimestre de 2022, com 205 mil toneladas. Além da Alemanha, a CSN tem presença em Portugal por meio da produtora de aços planos Lusosider. A empresa ainda não havia citado publicamente a SWT como alvo de venda, embora executivos da companhia tenham citado nos últimos trimestres que a CSN estava aberta a avaliar alternativas e parcerias para suas operações siderúrgicas. Em outros mercados internacionais, a CSN chegou a ter usinas nos Estados Unidos, mas vendeu esses ativos para norte-americana Steel Dynamics (STLD.O) em 2018. No Brasil, a CSN anunciou em agosto que recebeu propostas vinculantes por sua produtora de [USN:L6N4470LD TEXT:"cimento"]. Na época, as fontes afirmaram à Reuters que as principais concorrentes pela CSN Cimentos eram a chinesa Huaxin (600801.SS) e um consórcio formado por Votorantim e Cementir (CEMI.MI) , de origem italiana, e que as propostas deveriam ultrapassar os R$10 bilhões. A CSN terminou junho com alavancagem financeira de 3,49 vezes e dívida líquida de R$42,1 bilhões.

item.title: Boarded windows and evacuations as major hurricane nears US Gulf coast
item.description: Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing with it life-threatening storm surge and 115 mph (185 kph) winds.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hay
item.content:encoded: Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing with it life-threatening storm surge and 115 mph (185 kph) winds. Tens of thousands of people in Florida's Panhandle and Alabama's Gulf Coast faced mandatory evacuation orders. Local television stations showed roads packed with vehicles heading north, away from the water. The Category 3 Isaias, the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season for the United States, was expected to make landfall between Mobile, Alabama, and Grayton Beach in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Center. The 90-mile (145 km) stretch of coast is known for brilliant-white sand beaches, with some areas packed with vacation homes next to small coastal towns like Destin, Florida. "If you've been asked to evacuate, get out now, conditions are only going to deteriorate," NHC Director Michael Brennan told Fox Weather on Friday. "That surge is going to come in after dark, that's not a place you are going to want to be in." Scientists say human-caused climate change has warmed the Gulf of Mexico, possibly intensifying hurricanes like Isaias. The storm will pack sustained winds capable of extensive structural damage to beach houses, though modern homes built to strict coastal codes may remain standing. Storm surge of up to 9 feet (2.7 meters) was forecast around the Alabama-Florida border. President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45V0XC TEXT:"canceled"] a planned trip to Alabama on Saturday for the Georgia vs. Alabama college football game, as the hurricane is expected to affect Tuscaloosa, the city where the contest was set to be played. Up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain was expected in localized areas of the Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend area. Oil companies have evacuated personnel from 129 [USN:L1N45V0PT TEXT:"oil and gas"] production platforms, representing 35% of the 371 staffed platforms in the Gulf of Mexico. Hurricane-force winds were expected as far as 100 miles inland in southern Alabama, possibly triggering tornadoes. Some 2 to 5 inches (5 to 13 cm) of rain were expected across the US Southeast as far north as the southern Appalachian Mountains and coastal areas of the Carolinas.

item.title: Taxed pitching staffs will decide Game 5 between Guardians, White Sox
item.description: CLEVELAND -- The American League Division Series has provided a roller coaster of emotions for the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- The American League Division Series has provided a roller coaster of emotions for the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox. Road teams have won the first four contests, setting up a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday night. Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams (0-0, 3.00 ERA) takes on White Sox right-hander Sean Burke (1-0, 3.86 ERA) in a battle of traditional starters. The Tampa Bay Rays await the victor in the AL Championship Series. "Obviously, it's an honor to be able to start this game and go out there and do my thing for the guys," said Burke, who allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings as the bulk reliever in Game 2. "I empty the tank every single time I'm out there, so this is no different. I'm giving 100% of everything I have." Williams had been penciled in three days earlier, but his availability became a question mark after he came out of the bullpen for the final three outs Thursday in Cleveland's 9-5 win in Game 4. According to Guardians manager Stephen Vogt, "The Big Rig" earned the right to make the decision himself. The staff ace did so shortly after walking off the field. "The body feels good right now, been in the training room all morning just figuring it out," said Williams, who threw 18 pitches in his first career relief outing. "I throw a (bullpen session) on those (specific off) days, and everybody knows it. Just being able to feel the mound in a game-like situation is even better at that point." It's essentially a rematch of Game 2, when Williams struck out 11 over five-plus innings and allowed two runs. Burke was the winning pitcher as Chicago rallied for a 4-3 triumph Monday. Burke has been brilliant against the Guardians this season, going 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA over 22 2/3 innings. He has won in Cleveland in his last two matchups, giving up one earned run in 10 1/3 frames. "I've really seen his confidence grow," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "It's how he finishes his pitches, how he walks around the mound after he gets an out. Sean is a guy that's got the right mentality to figure out a way to get it done." Williams' work against the White Sox has been a mixed bag, with an 0-1 record and a 3.76 ERA in six total appearances (five starts). He has struck out 40 over 26 1/3 innings and averaged 5.1 innings per start. "Gavin wants the ball, we want him to have the ball, and it's his game," Vogt said. "The game will tell us when it's time to move on, or maybe he takes it the whole way. We don't know. We've got to get there and find out." Of more concern for Cleveland is closer Cade Smith, who pitched two innings in Game 3 and was going to do the same in Game 4 until faltering in the ninth. The MLB saves co-leader tossed 50 total pitches. White Sox counterpart Grant Taylor, who earned saves in the first two games, declared himself good to go after a disastrous four-run, zero-out night in Game 4. Smith, however, spent Friday receiving treatment at the ballpark and opted out of a scheduled press conference. "I don't know if it's something that we can push to a ton of pitches with Cade," Vogt admitted. "But when you have to play three straight elimination games, there's going to be some high volume." The series began with a pair of games in Cleveland, where White Sox pitchers held the hosts to seven total hits. Munetaka Murakami and Braden Montgomery provided the go-ahead RBIs. Chicago's dreams of clinching in the Windy City were dashed by Jose Ramirez and Jo Adell, who each totaled five RBIs as the Central Division-champion Guardians scored nine runs in both Games 3 and 4. As a result, the division rivals will contest the 40th ALDS Game 5 under the current format. Home teams are 18-21 all-time. "We're obviously thinking about the game and the situation a lot," Cleveland second baseman Travis Bazzana said. "You'll get some butterflies, some nerves, and a little bit of a good heart rate as we get closer and closer to game time." --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Broncos OC Davis Webb disappointed to lose play-calling role
item.description: Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb didn't envision getting only four games to show off his abilities as a play-caller.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb didn't envision getting only four games to show off his abilities as a play-caller. Webb said Friday "it's not ideal" to be stripped of the duties so early in the season. Head coach Sean Payton has taken over and will call the plays for Sunday's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers. By all accounts, that is a small sample size for a change to be made when it comes to a new play-caller. "Luckily that's not my job, that's (Payton's) job," Webb said Friday. "I think he answered that. I think the world of him, how we've gone about it ... it's not ideal, but in the same breath, we're 2-2 in the first four games, our first four opponents were a combined 13-3 to start the season. Welcome to the league." The Broncos rank 27th in scoring offense (18.5 points per game) and 28th in total offense (280.3 yards per game) while scoring 20 or fewer points in three of their first four games. Criticisms about Webb began immediately when Denver was routed 31-10 in its season opener on Monday Night Football by the Kansas City Chiefs. Others question Webb being in the role since he is just 31 years old and only in his fourth season of coaching. Webb felt he was ready for the play-calling role when he was promoted to offensive coordinator in the offseason. "I taught myself early to think about the best- and worst-case scenarios," Webb said. "And if you're OK with both, then take that job on. It is what it is, nothing I can do about it now except be the best offensive coordinator I can be and that's what I'm trying to do." Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has passed for 819 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions this season. He is completing 60% of his passes after hitting on 63.4% last season and 66.3% as a rookie in 2024. Webb threw 40 NFL passes - all in his lone start in 2022 for the New York Giants. He spent six NFL seasons between active rosters and practice squads with the Giants (2017, 2022), New York Jets (2018) and Buffalo Bills (2019-21). He was a third-round pick in the 2017 NFL Draft. Webb played three seasons at Texas Tech (2013-15) and had a monster 2016 season at Cal with 4,295 yards and 37 touchdowns against 12 interceptions. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kremlin says Putin in phone call with Trump downplays immediate Ukraine talks resumption
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told US President Donald Trump on Friday that Kyiv had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election, the Kremlin said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin told US President Donald Trump on Friday that Kyiv had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election, the Kremlin said. Trump has so far unsuccessfully tried to broker a peace deal to end the war in Ukraine , which started with Russia's invasion in February 2022. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a [USN:L1N45U0GU TEXT:"dangerous stalemate"] and the United States will keep working toward a settlement to end the conflict. Putin had said that Moscow had been [USN:L1N45H0MX TEXT:"ready to resume"] negotiations with Kyiv after last month's Russian parliamentary elections, but Ukraine launched attacks on Moscow and hit polling stations, putting the peace process in jeopardy, according to him. "By launching a massive drone attack on Moscow, other cities and polling stations, as well as on specific individuals involved in organising the election, on the main voting day, the Kyiv regime effectively disrupted the possibility of an immediate resumption of the negotiation process," Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said about the call with Trump. "And now, as the president said, we will consider when those negotiations can be resumed," he added, referring to trilateral negotiations involving the US, Russia and Ukraine. Ushakov also said Putin and Trump discussed major economic initiatives during the phone call, including potential supplies of Russian fuel. Trump said earlier on Friday after the call with Putin that Russia had agreed to immediately [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"supply diesel"] to US and global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections next month, although analysts said the amounts would likely not reduce prices greatly.

item.title: Sem orientação clara da campanha, base pró-Lula se mobiliza nas ruas e nas redes
item.description: Cinco dias depois de terminado o primeiro turno, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula fez nesta sexta-feira sua primeira agenda externa, mas enquanto seu partido tenta se reorganizar depois da derrota inicial para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), grupos regionais, estudantes, influenciadores e organizações de fãs, os chamados fandoms, foram para as ruas, mesmo sem orientações claras.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Cinco dias depois de terminado o primeiro turno, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula fez nesta sexta-feira sua primeira agenda externa, mas enquanto seu partido tenta se reorganizar depois da derrota inicial para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), grupos regionais, estudantes, influenciadores e organizações de fãs, os chamados fandoms, foram para as ruas, mesmo sem orientações claras. Já desde terça-feira, passada a derrota por quase 2 pontos percentuais, grupos começaram a se organizar pela internet. Na quarta-feira, milhares de estudantes foram às ruas no Rio de Janeiro contra a eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro. Desde então, houve manifestações de estudantes em pelo menos 10 Estados. No domingo, na Paulista, outra marcha está sendo organizada pela União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE), apoiada por fã-clubes de centenas de artistas pop, que foram às redes declarar apoio ao presidente e se oferecer para ocupar as redes em defesa da campanha do presidente. "Vocês viram as manifestações dos estudantes. São iniciativas próprias, voluntárias, de quem não quer o risco desse país voltar ao modelo que teve no governo Bolsonaro", disse o senador Camilo Santana, que se incorporou à coordenação da campanha neste segundo turno. O que parece ser um ponto positivo, no entanto, acaba por dar razão a queixas de aliados: quase uma semana se passou das três de campanha nesse segundo turno e pouca ou quase nenhuma orientação veio da coordenação da campanha, que tenta se reestruturar com novos nomes depois de enormes críticas de aliados à condução da campanha no primeiro turno. "Não recebemos nada, mas não vamos parar. A gente está fazendo o que pode, tem mobilização todo dia", diz uma fonte de campanha regional. Só não tem o presidente. Lula fez nesta sexta-feira uma caminhada em Ceilândia, cidade-satélite de Brasília, seu primeiro evento de campanha. No sábado, tem outro evento no Rio Grande do Norte, mas a agenda para por aí. No domingo, quem deve ir à Paulista com os estudantes é o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin. Camilo Santana afirma que o presidente irá a Minas, São Paulo e vários Estados, mas a agenda ainda não está definida. "Não tem como ir a todos os Estados", disse. Um parlamentar que participou das reuniões esta semana disse à Reuters que, mesmo sem orientações específicas, os parlamentares e candidatos, mesmo os que não foram eleitos, estão mantendo suas estruturas para tentar ajudar na campanha nacional como podem. Na quinta-feira, em São Paulo, o ministro da Secretaria-Geral da Presidência, Guilherme Boulos, o ex-ministro Fernando Haddad, candidato derrotado ao governo de São Paulo e diversos deputados eleitos fizeram uma "plenária de mobilização, na zona central de São Paulo, para organizar mutirões de panfletagem. No mesmo dia, à tarde, Haddad foi à Paulista distribuir panfletos. É nas redes que a interação subiu, com diversos grupos e influenciadores não apenas declarando voto, mas usando o alcance para marcar manifestações e falar não apenas de propostas, mas do que veem como riscos de um futuro governo Flávio Bolsonaro e dividindo estratégias para mudar votos.

item.title: Kalshi probes suspicious trades tied to Trump press secretary pick, WSJ reports
item.description: Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson. Kalshi declined to comment on the report. Here are some details: At least three small wagers were placed before news of Zacharia's selection emerged, potentially netting traders thousands of dollars in profits, the Journal reported. A $19 bet placed late on Thursday is set to pay $1,896, while wagers of about $74 and $80 placed on Friday are expected to pay $3,689 and $4,023, respectively. Zacharia, a conservative commentator who previously worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security, had been given about a 1% chance of securing the role on Kalshi before the announcement. Prediction markets, where users wager on outcomes ranging from sporting contests to world events, have faced growing scrutiny over the risk of traders profiting from inside information. In July, Trump's teleprompter operator came under investigation by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission over potential insider trading.

item.title: Two Sidus Space directors resign, citing governance disagreements
item.description: Satellite technology firm Sidus Space said on Friday two directors had resigned from its board, citing disagreements over governance and management practices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Satellite technology firm Sidus Space (SIDU.O) said on Friday two directors had resigned from its board, citing disagreements over governance and management practices. The company said it disagreed with the assertions made by the directors in their resignation letters. Here are some details: Tiffany Norwood and Kelle Wendling resigned from Sidus Space's board effective October 6, according to a regulatory filing. Norwood, chair of the audit committee and a member of the corporate governance and nominating committee, cited "a number of concerns and disagreements", including the handling of a confidential complaint brought to her and other committee chairs. Wendling, a member of the audit, compensation, and corporate governance and nominating committees, said she resigned after considering matters related to the company's management and governance. Sidus Space included both directors' resignation letters in the regulatory filing. "I have previously raised concerns regarding these matters through the appropriate Board and committee processes, and those concerns remain unresolved," Wendling said in her letter. The company said it had notified Norwood and Wendling of its disclosures and given them an opportunity to state whether they agreed with its response.

item.title: Lens hang on for much needed win to climb up Ligue 1 standings
item.description: RC Lens claimed only their second Ligue 1 win of the season on Friday after holding off second-placed Olympique Lyonnais for a 2-1 home victory.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RC Lens claimed only their second Ligue 1 win of the season on Friday after holding off second-placed Olympique Lyonnais for a 2-1 home victory. Veteran striker Florian Sotoca put the hosts ahead 10 minutes before the break and left back Matthieu Udol added the second 14 minutes from time as Lens dominated the game. But when Udol was dismissed in the 84th minute, it offered Lyon a lifeline and they immediately pulled one back when teenager Khalis Merah took advantage of a defensive slip. However, they proved unable to score a second goal and preserve their unbeaten start to the season. Lens were last season’s runners-up but had made a slow start to the new campaign after seeing coach Pierre Sage leave for Crystal Palace and then firing his replacement Dino Toppmoeller four matches into the season. Friday’s win was a first victory for new coach Yannick Cahuzac in his second game since taking over. Success for Lens saw them leap from 15th spot to seventh in the standings, with seven points. Lyon remain second with 11 points.

item.title: Declaran culpables a tres por homicidio surfistas extranjeros norte México; fiscalía pide 210 años en prisión
item.description: Un juez mexicano declaró culpables el viernes a tres hombres por el asesinato de dos surfistas australianos y un estadounidense en 2024, en un destino turístico de la costa del Pacífico, en el norte del país, informó una fuente del Poder Judicial del estado Baja California.
item.dc:creator: Lizbeth Diaz
item.content:encoded: Un juez mexicano declaró culpables el viernes a tres hombres por el asesinato de dos surfistas australianos y un estadounidense en 2024, en un destino turístico de la costa del Pacífico, en el norte del país, informó una fuente del Poder Judicial del estado Baja California. Los hermanos australianos Jake y Callum Robinson, de entonces 30 y 33 años, respectivamente, y su amigo Carter Rhoad, de 30, realizaban un viaje de práctica de surf en una playa del municipio Ensenada, a unos cientos de kilómetros de la frontera con Estados Unidos. Al caer la noche, en la zona despoblada donde acampaban, fueron asesinados a tiros tras resistirse a un asalto. "El fallo fue condenatorio", dijo la fuente del Poder Judicial estatal. "La lectura de la sentencia será viernes 16", agregó. Los acusados fueron declarados culpables de homicidio calificado cometido con premeditación, alevosía y ventaja, así como de robo con violencia y robo de vehículo de motor con violencia, indicó la fuente. Más tarde el viernes, la fiscal del estado Elena Andrade dijo que la dependencia a su cargo está solicitando hasta 210 años de prisión para "cada uno de los agresores", pero que al final será el juez quien determinará la pena. La funcionaria agregó que se mantendría en contacto tanto con familiares como con representantes consultares de las víctimas. Los cuerpos de los extranjeros fueron encontrados días después de que su familia reportó su desaparición -en abril de 2024- dentro de un pozo de agua con heridas de bala en la cabeza. La camioneta en que viajaban, además, fue hallada calcinada en otro punto a varios kilómetros de la zona en que ocurrieron los hechos. La fiscalía había solicitado previamente una pena de hasta 150 años de prisión para Jesús Gerardo "N", alias "El Kekas", señalado como el principal responsable del crimen. El 19 de noviembre, Gisell Silva, entonces novia de "El Kekas", fue condenada a 20 años de prisión por su participación en el caso. La mujer de entonces 23 años fue detenida pocos días después de que fueron encontrados los cadáveres de los extranjeros. Martin y Debra Robinson, padres de los hermanos, viajaron a México para asistir al juicio. Ellos han descrito lo que vivieron tras la muerte de sus hijos como "un infierno" y una experiencia "increíblemente difícil".

item.title: Mexican court finds three men guilty of 2024 killing of Australian, US surfers
item.description: A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a source at the court told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a source at the court told Reuters. Jesus Gerardo Garcia, known as "El Kekas," and the co-defendants identified simply as Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N," were found guilty of aggravated homicide, violent robbery and vehicle theft by a Baja California court. The prosecution had sought sentences of up to 150 years against the suspects. According to the same source at the state court, the sentence will be announced on October 16. Brothers Callum, 33, and Jake Robinson, 30, and American Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, were camping and surfing near Punta San Jose, about 80 km (50 miles) south of Ensenada, when they were reported missing in late April 2024. After a days-long search, aided by the FBI, their bodies were found on May 3 at the bottom of a well. The victims were each found with gunshot wounds in the head, authorities said. Prosecutors said the accused had attempted to carjack the tourists, who were shot when they tried to resist. Their truck was later found burned nearby. Martin and Debra Robinson, the Robinsons' parents, traveled from their hometown of Perth to attend the four-week trial. Rhoad's widowed fiancee, Natalie Weirtz, spoke via video call from the United States. In November 2025 Gisell Silva, Garcia's then-girlfriend, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for her involvement in the case. The woman, who was 23 at the time, was arrested a few days after the bodies of the victims were found. While the Ensenada area is considered relatively safe, Baja California ranks among Mexico’s most violent states. Following the killings, the US State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to the state due to crime and kidnapping risks.

item.title: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
item.description: Amazon on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its first tablet computers featuring the voice assistant.
item.dc:creator: Greg Bensinger
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its [USN:L6N45T1AE TEXT:"first tablet computers"] featuring the voice assistant. Daniel Rausch, a 17-year Amazon veteran who has served as vice president of Alexa and Echo for over three years, is stepping away from the unit next month, Amazon said in response to a Reuters inquiry. Rausch, who has served as the face of Alexa at events and global launches, will return in another capacity in the devices and services division in 2027. In his place, Amazon will install Aidan Marcuss, currently the vice president of Fire TV, advertising and the Amazon appstore. Marcuss joined Amazon from Microsoft (MSFT.O) in early 2025. He oversaw the release of a new Fire TV stick last month, which has garnered mixed reviews. Kevin Keith, a product and marketing vice president, will keep that role but also take on Marcuss' responsibilities for the time being, Amazon said. The company declined to provide additional detail about the changes. Alexa has been a consistent money-loser for Amazon since its release in 2014. Amazon spent several years developing a new version of the voice assistant offering generative AI that can respond to longer prompts. The service is featured in the new Alexa Tablets announced on Thursday that Amazon has priced as a high-end product compared with prior Fire tablets that were inexpensive. Alexa+, as the latest version is known, is included in the $139-per-year Prime membership or for $20 monthly as a standalone service.

item.title: Plantio de soja no Brasil vai a quase 20% da área, em ritmo recorde, diz Pátria
item.description: O plantio da safra de soja 2026/27 do Brasil atingiu 19,77% da área total estimada, marcando o ritmo mais acelerado de semeadura já observado no país, com chuvas favorecendo as atividades nos campos, de acordo com dados da consultoria Pátria AgroNegócios divulgados nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O plantio da safra de soja 2026/27 do Brasil atingiu 19,77% da área total estimada, marcando o ritmo mais acelerado de semeadura já observado no país, com chuvas favorecendo as atividades nos campos, de acordo com dados da consultoria Pátria AgroNegócios divulgados nesta sexta-feira. Na mesma época do ano passado, os trabalhos cobriam 12,86% da área, enquanto a média dos últimos cinco anos para o período é de 11,55%. "Estamos vivenciando o mais acelerado ritmo de plantio da safra de verão brasileira", afirmou a consultoria em relatório. Segundo a Pátria, o avanço tem sido favorecido pela chegada precoce e pelos volumes satisfatórios de chuvas nas principais regiões produtoras. A aceleração dos trabalhos com a soja é importante para as culturas de segunda safra se desenvolverem dentro da melhor janela climática. Além disso, pode permitir que colheita da soja seja antecipada, se as condições climáticas continuarem favoráveis, de forma geral, no maior produtor e exportador da oleaginosa. "Abrindo bem a janela para segunda safra, até o momento. Estamos falando de soja plantada agora que entra em colheita em janeiro, excelente para colocar milho no chão", disse o diretor da consultoria, Matheus Pereira. Na última semana, os destaques foram Mato Grosso, Goiás e Mato Grosso do Sul, que registraram rápido avanço dos trabalhos de campo. A consultoria citou que 33,3% da safra já foi plantada em Mato Grosso, maior produtor brasileiro. O número está em linha com o anunciado mais cedo pelo Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea), que indicou um [USN:L1N45V0UW TEXT:"salto"] de mais de 20 pontos percentuais na semeadura do Estado. Já no Paraná, o plantio evoluiu pouco em razão do excesso de precipitações, conforme havia alertado o Departamento de Economia Rural (Deral). Contudo, o Estado sulista está adiantado nos trabalhos de semeadura, com mais de 40% da área já plantada, após as chuvas terem chegado mais cedo este ano. O diretor da Pátria disse ainda que, apesar da evolução no plantio, em partes de Mato Grosso, como o noroeste, alguns tiveram de replantar devido a condições desfavoráveis para o desenvolvimento. "Centro-Norte do MT está precisando de chuvas. Pode ser um problema se novas rodadas não chegarem na próxima semana.", acrescentou ele.

item.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones finally puts her Welsh accent to work in show 'Kill Jackie'
item.description: It was not until Catherine Zeta-Jones began working on the Prime Video series "Kill Jackie" that she had an epiphany: for the first time in her career, she would be playing a character with a Welsh accent, matching her own.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway, Rollo Ross
item.content:encoded: It was not until Catherine Zeta-Jones began working on the Prime Video series "Kill Jackie" that she had an epiphany: for the first time in her career, she would be playing a character with a Welsh accent, matching her own. "Jackie Price is Welsh. Even her name sounds Welsh," Zeta-Jones told Reuters, referring to the former drug dealer turned art dealer she portrays in the series. "Once that was in my head, there was no going back. I have to be honest, I got a little jealous of other actors who've never had to do accents all their lives," she added. The Oscar-winning actor said the realization prompted her to reflect on a career spent almost exclusively playing characters with accents different from her own. From using an American accent in the 2004 film "The Terminal" to adopting a Scottish accent in the 2008 film "Death Defying Acts," the Welsh actor has portrayed characters from around the world. But the accent was not the only aspect of "Kill Jackie," which premiered on Prime Video in Britain, Canada and some other countries on October 2, that drew her to the role. It premiered in the US on AMC+. Zeta-Jones was also captivated by the character herself: Jackie Price, a former cocaine dealer who lives a luxurious life selling art through tax loopholes. After 20 years of anonymity, Jackie's quiet existence is upended when a group of elite hitmen known as The Seven Demons is hired to kill her. The series also stars Daniel Ings, Julian Rhind-Tutt, Sidse Babett Knudsen and Christine Adams. "She speaks before she thinks, and she says what she thinks," Zeta-Jones said of the qualities that made her connect with the character. The "Ocean's Twelve" actor said she admires Jackie's unfiltered nature, particularly because her own demeanor tends to be more serious and restrained.

item.title: Lockheed Martin unveils PAC-3 Edge interceptor designed to counter hypersonic threats
item.description: Lockheed Martin on Friday unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a missile interceptor designed to defend against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the US military looks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) on Friday unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a missile interceptor designed to defend against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the US military looks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats. Growing demand for air and missile defense systems amid conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East has strained US weapons stockpiles, prompting the US Army to award Lockheed Martin a contract [USN:L1N43V1ND TEXT:"worth up to $58.6 billion"] in July to ramp up production of PAC-3 interceptors. Lockheed Martin said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls and a multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman, enhancing the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, at longer ranges and higher altitudes. "The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, president of missiles and fire control at Lockheed Martin, told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE." In January, Lockheed Martin [USN:L4N3Y714G TEXT:"signed"] a seven-year framework agreement with the US Department of Defense to expand production of its PAC-3 missile interceptors, aiming to increase annual manufacturing capacity to 2,000 units from about 600.

item.title: Fullkrug haunts former side as Bremen battle for 2-2 draw at Dortmund
item.description: Niclas Fullkrug returned to haunt former club Borussia Dortmund as Werder Bremen came back from two goals down to earn a 2-2 draw on Friday, with the Bundesliga leaders dropping points for the first time this season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Niclas Fullkrug returned to haunt former club Borussia Dortmund as Werder Bremen came back from two goals down to earn a 2-2 draw on Friday, with the Bundesliga leaders dropping points for the first time this season. Dortmund were cruising 2-0 with two minutes remaining but somehow contrived to draw the game, denying them the chance to win their first five league games in a campaign for the first time since 2015. Dortmund move to 13 points from five matches and have opened up a three-point lead at the top of the table over second-placed Bayern Munich, who have a game in hand. All four goals in the game came in the final 10 minutes as Daniel Svensson and Nico Schlotterbeck scored in front of the Yellow Wall, who were left feeling a little 'green' by the end of the evening. That looked to have put the home side in control of the contest, only for Ludovit Reis and Fullkrug to put on a late show for the visitors. Fabio Silva’s miskicked attempted shot fell kindly for Svensson to score from 10-yards on 80 minutes. Nico Schlotterbeck had pulled out of Germany’s squad with injury ahead of the international break, so it was a surprise to see him starting for Dortmund. His towering header from Joey Veerman’s corner made it 2-0. That looked like game over, but Ludovit Reis’ superb low strike from outside the box pulled a goal back and Fullkrug made it 2-2 for the most unlikely of comebacks. Dortmund coach Niko Kovac will be seething and left wondering how his side capitulated in the closing minutes. If they are to challenge Bayern for the title this season, they cannot drop points in this fashion at home.

item.title: Eztec eleva lançamentos em 53% no 3º tri
item.description: A construtora e incorporadora Eztec anunciou nesta sexta-feira alta de 52,9% nos lançamentos de imóveis no terceiro trimestre ante o mesmo período de 2025, para R$726,5 milhões, segundo prévia de resultados do período divulgada ao mercado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A construtora e incorporadora Eztec (EZTC3.SA) anunciou nesta sexta-feira alta de 52,9% nos lançamentos de imóveis no terceiro trimestre ante o mesmo período de 2025, para R$726,5 milhões, segundo prévia de resultados do período divulgada ao mercado. Os lançamentos corresponderam a três empreendimentos no período, feitos na região metropolitana de São Paulo. Segundo a prévia, com o terceiro trimestre, a Eztec, que tradicionalmente é focada em segmentos de médio e alto padrões, acumulou nos nove primeiros meses deste ano R$2,4 bilhões em lançamentos, crescimento de 53,3% sobre um ano antes e recorde para a empresa no período. Desse total, R$411 milhões foram voltados ao segmento econômico, que tem sido impulsionado no país nos últimos anos pelo programa federal Minha Casa Minha Vida. No acumulado de janeiro a setembro de 2025, os lançamentos da Eztec no segmento econômico tinham sido de R$110 milhões. A companhia registrou vendas líquidas praticamente estáveis, a R$522,7 milhões entre julho e o final de setembro, recuo de 0,6% na comparação anual. No acumulado do ano até o mês passado, as vendas somaram R$1,8 bilhão, alta de 29,2% sobre o mesmo período de 2025 e também recorde para a empresa. A Eztec terminou setembro com estoque total de R$3,5 bilhões, sendo R$1,1 bilhão em estoque pronto, R$1,36 bilhão em construção e R$1,1 bilhão de lançamentos.

item.title: Base Electron confidentially files for US IPO
item.description: Power infrastructure firm Base Electron said on Friday it had confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Power infrastructure firm Base Electron said on Friday it had confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering. The confidential filing comes as interest in AI-linked infrastructure remains strong, though investors are increasingly scrutinising valuations, capital needs and backlog quality. Here are some details: The number of shares to be offered and the price range for the proposed offering have not yet been determined, the company said. Applied Digital (APLD.O) formed Base Electron to supply power to the technology firm's AI campuses under separate agreements. Base Electron develops, owns and operates energy infrastructure serving data centers, AI facilities and large industrial users. Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC. In March, Base Electron approved a $2.4 billion [USN:L6N3ZS0X4 TEXT:"agreement"] with Babcock & Wilcox for equipment to support a 1.2-gigawatt power project serving Applied Digital's artificial intelligence campuses.
