item.title: Guardians' Gavin Williams starting Game 5 vs. White Sox after closing Game 4
item.description: Gavin Williams will start the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series against the Chicago White Sox on Saturday in Cleveland, two days after he closed out the Game 4 victory.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gavin Williams will start the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series against the Chicago White Sox on Saturday in Cleveland, two days after he closed out the Game 4 victory. The right-hander needed 18 pitches to record three outs and finish the 9-5 road victory on Thursday when the Guardians evened the best-of-five series. Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said Friday that Williams recovered fine from the cameo appearance. "So Gavin is ready to go tomorrow," Vogt said. "Feels good today. So we will obviously see how he's doing tomorrow." Williams also started Game 2 on Monday when he struck out 11 in five-plus innings. He gave up two runs, four hits and three walks and received a no-decision in Cleveland's 4-3 loss. Vogt said Williams will operate under normal conditions and able to pitch as long as necessary. "I think we'll be watching the game," Vogt said. "I think we'll be monitoring it. But I think, again, it's a Game 5, win or go home. Gavin wants the ball. We want him to have the ball, and it's his game. "And the game will tell us when it's time to move on, or maybe he takes it the whole way. We don't know. We gotta get there and find out." Williams, 27, went 14-8 during the regular season with a 3.76 ERA and 248 strikeouts in 32 starts. Right-hander Sean Burke will pitch for Chicago. Burke, 26, earned the victory in the bulk relief role against Williams in Game 2. He gave up one run, one hit, one walk and struck out six in 5 1/3 innings. Burke went 11-7 with a 3.34 ERA and 185 strikeouts in 32 appearances (27 starts) in the regular season. Burke also has his sights on pitching as long as he can on Saturday. "I empty the tank every single time I'm out there," Burke said Friday. "This is no different for me. Every single game I go out there, I'm giving 100 percent of everything I have, and I don't think tomorrow is any different. "I think that I'll just embrace this moment. I love moments like these. I love being able to pitch in the big game. And just the fact that the coaching staff and the team trust me to go out there and do my thing tomorrow just means the world to me." The White Sox won the first two games of the series in Cleveland before the Guardians returned serve and took two in Chicago. --Field Level Media

item.title: GTCR, Elliott in advanced talks to buy CCC Intelligent Solutions, source says
item.description: Private equity firm GTCR and activist investor Elliott Investment Management are in advanced talks to acquire software provider CCC Intelligent Solutions , a source familiar with the matter said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Private equity firm GTCR and activist investor Elliott Investment Management are in advanced talks to acquire software provider CCC Intelligent Solutions (CCC.O) , a source familiar with the matter said on Friday. Shares of the company, which provides software that helps auto insurers, repair shops, automakers and parts suppliers manage operations, rose about 13% in extended trading after Bloomberg News first reported the news. A deal could be announced as soon as next week but a final agreement had not been reached, the source said, without disclosing financial details CCC and GTCR did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment, while Elliott declined to comment Bloomberg News had reported in August that online vehicle auctioneer Copart (CPRT.O) was in talks to acquire CCC In July, Reuters had [USN:L6N43B182 TEXT:"reported"] that CCC was exploring a sale and that the Chicago-based company had hired Morgan Stanley to advise on the process and reached out to potential buyers, including private equity firms Advent International, which acquired CCC in 2017 and took the company public through a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company in 2021, exited its investment in 2025 through a series of secondary share offerings, including the sale of its remaining stake

item.title: Eagles release QB Andy Dalton, rule out star RB Saquon Barkley vs. Jags
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles released backup quarterback Andy Dalton on Friday among a flurry of roster moves ahead of their game Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Eagles released backup quarterback Andy Dalton on Friday among a flurry of roster moves ahead of their game Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles (2-2) ruled out star running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) as well as safety Marcus Epps (groin), center/guard Drew Kendall (knee) and wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Marquise Brown (ankle). Those five players did not practice all week, nor did outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who is listed as questionable for the game against the Jaguars (3-1). Starting quarterback Jalen Hurts made his first appearance on the practice report this season with a calf injury but was a full participant with no injury status for Sunday. Philadelphia obtained Dalton from the Carolina Panthers on March 18 for a 2027 seventh-round pick. He played in one game, filling in when Hurts was being evaluated for a possible concussion. Dalton threw his lone pass for an interception in a 27-7 loss at Chicago on Sept. 28. Dalton was demoted behind Tanner McKee, now the primary backup, with rookie Cole Payton, a fifth-round pick this year out of North Dakota State, also on the roster. ESPN reported that Dalton could be a candidate for the Eagles' practice squad. Dalton, who turns 39 on Oct. 29, served as a backup for Carolina for the previous three seasons under starter Bryce Young. He spent the first nine years of his career with the Cincinnati Bengals before having one-year stints with the Dallas Cowboys, Bears and New Orleans Saints. In 180 games (169 starts), Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns and 152 interceptions with a career passer rating of 87.4. He has a career record of 84-83-2 as a starter and is a three-time Pro Bowl selection. McKee, 26, has played in a total of six games (two starts) for the Eagles in parts of the previous two seasons and has completed 54 of 88 passes (61.4%) for 597 yards, five TDs and one pick. Philadelphia selected him in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Eagles also announced on Friday that they have signed center Jake Majors and running back Carson Steele from the practice squad to the active roster and placed defensive tackle Uar Bernard on the practice squad injured list. Philadelphia became thin at running back when both Barkley and Tank Bigsby were injured in the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Bigsby was placed on IR with a core injury that requires surgery. Will Shipley is expected to serve as the lead back for the Eagles, with running back Dameon Pierce elevated to their 53-man roster earlier this week. --Field Level Media

item.title: Milho despenca em Chicago após USDA elevar a previsão de produtividade nos EUA
item.description: Os contratos futuros do milho negociados nos EUA despencaram em até o limite diário de negociação nesta sexta-feira e encerraram o dia com queda acentuada, depois que o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA (USDA) surpreendeu os operadores com um aumento inesperado na previsão para a safra norte-americana de 2026.
item.dc:creator: Karl Plume
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do milho negociados nos EUA despencaram em até o limite diário de negociação nesta sexta-feira e encerraram o dia com queda acentuada, depois que o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA (USDA) surpreendeu os operadores com um aumento inesperado na previsão para a safra norte-americana de 2026. O trigo seguiu a tendência de queda do milho, pressionado pelo aumento maior do que o esperado na previsão de estoques do USDA, enquanto a soja se recuperou de uma mínima de seis semanas e fechou o dia em alta. O USDA previu a safra de milho dos EUA em 16,034 bilhões de bushels, acima da estimativa de 15,800 bilhões divulgada há um mês, com um rendimento médio de 181,2 bushels por acre, acima dos 178,5 bpa anteriores. A revisão elevou a previsão de estoques no final da safra em 282 milhões de bushels em relação ao mês anterior. Analistas consultados pela Reuters esperavam, em média, que as estimativas de produção e rendimento médio diminuíssem devido às condições climáticas adversas para as culturas neste verão. "Foi um choque o USDA constatar o aumento da produção este ano. E, de fato, o aumento que eles registraram foi um choque realmente grande. Portanto, foi um relatório negativo, obviamente, e o mercado está reagindo de forma negativa", disse Jack Scoville, analista do The Price Group. Os futuros de milho para dezembro na bolsa de Chicago fecharam em queda de 20,50 centavos, atingindo a mínima de dois meses de US$4,7975 por bushel, após terem caído até o limite diário de 30 centavos após a divulgação do relatório. O contrato de referência registrou queda de 3,8% na semana. A soja para novembro fechou com alta de 4,50 centavos, a US$12,92 o bushel, recuperando-se de uma mínima de seis semanas registrada após o USDA elevar suas previsões de produção e estoques nos EUA. Na semana, o contrato mais negociado registrou alta de 1,1%. O contrato de trigo de dezembro da CBOT atingiu a menor cotação em dois meses e encerrou o dia com queda de 12,25 centavos, a US$6,71 por bushel. O contrato registrou sua sexta queda semanal consecutiva, recuando 1,8%.

item.title: US lifts sanctions on daughter of Myanmar military-linked businessman
item.description: The United States lifted on Friday sanctions on the daughter of a Myanmar businessman accused of supporting the country's military, according to the US Treasury Department's website, after she filed a suit seeking removal from the blacklist.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: The United States lifted on Friday sanctions on the daughter of a Myanmar businessman accused of supporting the country's military, according to the US Treasury Department's website, after she filed a suit seeking removal from the blacklist. The move comes after Reuters reported this week that the Trump administration had [USN:L6N45T16N TEXT:"opened talks with Myanmar's military-installed government"], reversing US policy that sought to isolate the generals who overthrew elected leaders in 2021. It was unclear if the decision to remove Myanmar national Theint Win Htet from the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) was a result of the talks. After the 2021 coup, former President Joe Biden's administration imposed sanctions on senior Myanmar military officers and companies it accused of providing support for the military junta, which triggered a nationwide civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million. The Treasury in January 2024 [USN:S0N3D107F TEXT:"targeted the "][USN:S0N3D107F TEXT:"Shwe Byain Phyu Group of Companies"], its founder Thein Win Zaw and his family, saying the company imported and distributed petroleum on behalf of the military and that the family owned at least 20 companies closely associated with the regime. Thein Win Zaw's adult daughter, Theint Win Htet, sued the Biden administration seeking her removal from the SDN List, but her case was dismissed in February 2025. The sanctions freeze any US assets of those targeted and generally bar Americans from dealing with them. The US in July 2025 [USN:L1N3TM01T TEXT:"lifted sanctions"] on several other Myanmar nationals and a firm under sanctions for aiding the military. Theint Win Htet filed a new complaint in July this year, arguing that she has no active role in her father's business affairs, adding that the sanctions had interrupted her studies in the US, where she completed a bachelor's degree at New York University and was enrolled in a master's program at Columbia University. "Plaintiff’s US credit cards have been blocked, her foreign bank accounts have been restricted, closed, or refused, and she has been unable to complete her university studies in the United States," said the complaint by Theint Win Htet, who said in the complaint she now lives with her mother in Bangkok. Her mother was removed from the sanctions list last year. Campaign group Justice For Myanmar denounced the US move at a time when it said the Myanmar military was escalating attacks on civilians. "It is deplorable that the US government continues to delist Myanmar cronies and their family members that provide funding for the junta's terror," the group said. Theint Win Htet's lawyer, Washington-based sanctions specialist Erich Ferrari, filed a notice with the US District Court for the District of Columbia on Friday voluntarily dismissing the lawsuit after her delisting. Ferrari declined to comment.

item.title: 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' expands with new prequel series 'Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos'
item.description: The world of successful TV franchise "Avatar: The Last Airbender" is expanding once again, with a new prequel series that will follow the story of a rebellious teenager Avatar — a being who controls the elements.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway
item.content:encoded: The world of successful TV franchise "Avatar: The Last Airbender" is expanding once again, with a new prequel series that will follow the story of a rebellious teenager Avatar — a being who controls the elements. Franchise co-creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko announced the animated TV series, titled "Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos," on Friday at New York Comic Con, with attendees getting a first look at Kuruk and his pet, Nikik. Kuruk aims to stay "one step ahead of his angry teacher, rowdy pirates, and chaotic spirits, all while helping the world in his own unique ways," said a statement from Skydance (SKYD.N) . The series is set to stream on Paramount+. No release date has been announced. The Asian-inspired "Avatar: The Last Airbender" franchise follows a world divided into four elemental nations, where the Avatar alone can control water, fire, earth and air to maintain balance. The original TV series has spawned two sequels, "The Legend of Korra," and "Avatar: Seven Havens." "Seven Havens" has been renewed for two additional seasons, the statement from Skydance said. DiMartino and Konietzko were involved in developing a live-action adaptation of the original "Avatar" series for Netflix (NFLX.O) before parting ways with the streamer in 2020, citing "creative differences." In 2021, they teamed with Nickelodeon to launch Avatar Studios, focused on expanding the universe of the original series through new films and television projects.

item.title: India's TCS senior staff will miss out on variable pay for September quarter, memo shows
item.description: Senior staff at India's Tata Consultancy Services will miss out on quarterly bonuses after the company failed to meet performance targets, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, the first time in at least two years all variable pay was withheld for some workers.
item.dc:creator: Sai B
item.content:encoded: Senior staff at India's Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) will miss out on quarterly bonuses after the company failed to meet performance targets, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, the first time in at least two years all variable pay was withheld for some workers. "For associates C3A grade and above, there will be no QVA (quarterly variable allowance) this quarter. This decision was taken after careful consideration as our performance for the quarter fell short of internal targets," said Sudeep Kunnumal, chief human resource officer in the memo. Associates in C3A and above grades are employees with typically 7-10 years of experience up to senior-level management. The junior-level employees will get 100% of the eligible pay, the memo added. Mails sent to TCS did not elicit a response. Employees, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said typically the company awards 50-100% of variable pay and it is the first time in at least two years that the company has explicitly said no bonuses shall be awarded. This comes as the country's largest IT firm reported its [USN:L6N45T0UF TEXT:"weakest"] September-quarter sequential revenue growth in three years, signaling continued pressure on traditional IT services demand even as AI-related revenue jumped nearly 20%. The uptick in AI revenue, however, was cheered by investors on Friday as the stock rose as much as 6.2%. India's $315 billion IT sector is also facing uncertainty stemming from the Trump administration as it [USN:S0N43501J TEXT:"suspended"] major IT outsourcers including TCS, Infosys (INFY.NS) , HCLTech (HCLT.NS) from a key green-card program on Thursday, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs.

item.title: Britain steps in to stop contentious Protestant parade in Northern Ireland
item.description: Britain's Northern Ireland minister on Friday overturned a decision by local authorities that granted a permit for a Protestant parade to pass through a Catholic area and triggered a two-week standoff that raised tensions in the region.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Ferguson
item.content:encoded: Britain's Northern Ireland minister on Friday overturned a decision by local authorities that granted a permit for a Protestant parade to pass through a Catholic area and triggered a two-week standoff that raised tensions in the region. Northern Ireland's Parades Commission last month [USN:L8N45H0SR TEXT:"allowed"] the Orange Order to march along the Garvaghy Road, a Catholic area in the mainly Protestant town of Portadown, for the first time since parades on the route were banned in 1998. Thousands of residents and protesters [USN:L1N45J00A TEXT:"stopped the parade"] from taking place. A small number of Orange Order members have since remained at the start of the route, while a round-the-clock police presence has kept them separated from protesters 1.5 kilometres (1 mile) away on the footpaths of the Garvaghy Road. Chris Bryant, Britain's secretary of state for Northern Ireland, said the region's police chief advised him that the parade could not go ahead without a major intervention from officers, which would carry "an unacceptable risk of serious injury, disorder and a wider contagion effect." That official advice triggered a mechanism whereby Bryant could step in to overturn the Parades Commission's ruling. "I have not taken this decision lightly," Bryant said in a statement, which also thanked the Orange Order for their peaceful and law-abiding approach throughout. A lawyer representing Alan Hynes, a local Orange Order member, said in a statement that his client would challenge the minister's decision in court and request that the matter be listed before a judge on Saturday. Bryant called for all protests, rallies and demonstrations to be stood down, saying there was no excuse for a continued ratcheting up of tensions. Annual attempts by the Orange Order to march through the area had triggered unrest across the region until the route was banned nearly three decades ago, in the same year that the Good Friday Agreement largely ended three decades of violence in Northern Ireland known as the "Troubles." "We don't view it as a victory but as a starting point because there are relationships within Portadown that need to be built and rebuilt," Breandán Mac Cionnaith, head of the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition, told national broadcaster RTE. The decision was welcomed by the Irish government and by Northern Ireland's largest Irish nationalist party Sinn Fein, whose leader in Northern Ireland Michelle O'Neill is due to be [USN:L1N45V0MJ TEXT:"interviewed by police"] for taking part in the protest. Sinn Fein's pro-British rivals, the Democratic Unionist Party, criticised the intervention, saying it was the "direct result of (Irish) Republican agitation, mobilisation and the looming threats of potential violence." DUP leader Gavin Robinson said in a statement, however, that his party would not walk away from the region's fragile devolved government, where it shares power with Sinn Fein.

item.title: Erik Prince's forces suffer battlefield loss in Congo, former UFC fighter among wounded, sources say
item.description: Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Donati
item.content:encoded: Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said. The frontline clash shows how Prince, an ally and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has taken on an expanded role in Congo through his company Vectus Global. The company, which also operates in Haiti and other parts of Africa, provides consulting and security services and previously [USN:L6N3XA0X0 TEXT:"helped Congo’s army"] secure the city of Uvira in South Kivu against Rwanda-backed rebels who control swathes of the east. A veteran special operator reported on his podcast earlier this week that former US Green Beret and Ultimate Fighting Championship contestant Tim Kennedy was injured in Congo. The involvement of Prince's forces and the number of casualties have not previously been reported. The attack in South Kivu on September 17 left about 20 dead and wounded, two sources working with Congo's government said. The dead included at least seven Congolese and a former member of New Zealand's Special Forces, while the wounded included Kennedy and another foreign contractor, the sources said. A Vectus Global representative declined to comment. The company has not previously suffered casualties in Congo, a source with direct knowledge of the operation said. One of the sources who works for Congo's government said that Rwandan forces backing the M23 rebels may have surprised them by tracking a drone used for surveillance operations to their location. Spokespeople for the Congolese and Rwandan governments and for the M23 did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Kennedy, the former mixed martial arts fighter, survived the attack with three gunshot wounds to the leg, three sources said, and is being treated at the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in the suburbs of Washington. Kennedy has a popular podcast channel and millions of followers on social media. Trump is a fan of UFC, [USN:L6N42N00Z TEXT:"hosting fights"] at the White House this year. The US State Department and Walter Reed declined to comment. Kennedy's parents did not respond to requests for comment. A Congolese security source, who said some 20 people were wounded and killed in the attack, added that villagers were likely among the casualties as well. Reuters spoke to at least 10 sources either with direct knowledge of the attack or briefed on the outcome. PRINCE TOOK EXPANDED ROLE IN CONGO'S CONFLICT Prince's initial mandate in Congo was to secure and improve revenue collection from the country's vast mineral reserves, which have been plundered for decades, fuelling relentless conflict in the east. But in January and early February, his forces deployed to Uvira after Washington helped broker a deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from the strategic town. The size of Prince's forces in Congo is unclear. One of the sources with direct knowledge of the attack said the Vectus team was travelling between locations when the ambush took place and its sophistication suggested Rwandan forces were involved. "It reinforces the need for DRC sovereignty to be restored. It's an incredibly dangerous place right now," the source said. Two other sources said the ambush was carried out by the Rwandan military. Prince is the founder of now-defunct private military firm Blackwater, some of whose members were pardoned in 2020 for killing Iraqi civilians. The State Department has said it does not have any contracts with Prince in Congo, though US officials have said they plan to work [USN:L1N43O0RW TEXT:"more closely with Vectus Global"] in Haiti. The deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from Uvira was part of [USN:L6N3XA0X0 TEXT:"wider agreements"] brokered by the Trump administration to try to end the conflict in eastern Congo. POPULAR PODCASTER Kennedy, a father of four, has posted his views on politics, culture, fitness and more on social media. He also runs a popular YouTube podcast in which he interviews UFC fighters, veterans, cultural disruptors and others. He has often posted about his family, including four young children. In late August, he posted about having "incredible conversations about what being a man means and what sacrifice really looks like" with his son. He did not disclose details about his upcoming trip to Congo. The United Nations and Western powers say Rwanda backs M23, even exercising command and control over the group. Rwanda denies this. Fighting in the decades-long conflict flared early last year, with M23 fighters making rapid gains in the east, which is rich in tantalum, gold, lithium and other minerals.

item.title: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
item.description: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among a string of incidents the AI company disclosed on Friday detailing Claude models' unsanctioned manipulation of some government websites.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among a string of incidents the AI company disclosed on Friday detailing Claude models' unsanctioned manipulation of some government websites. It is the first known instance in which a rogue AI appears to have tried to communicate a bogus tip to authorities, despite instructions not to create accounts or submit anything destructive, while not explicitly barred from submitting forms. The cases are the latest examples of rogue or undesired behavior by the AI models of tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI. They add fuel to national concerns about the fast-advancing technology amid reports of corporate network hacks by AI agents, and researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity. Many of the cases Anthropic revealed involved websites run by federal, state and local agencies. Anthropic said it briefed the White House and notified all the agencies involved, but did not disclose who those parties were. "Super intelligence companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm," FTC Director of Public Affairs Joe Gabriel Simonson said on X. This process was "not optional," he said, adding that the Super Intelligence Force would fulfill its responsibility. The FTC said Anthropic disclosed to the SI Force on Friday its late September discovery of incidents involving what the task force called "unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and other systems". TIP ATTRIBUTED TO AUTOMATED TEST PROCESS On Friday, Philadelphia police said Anthropic notified them of the spurious tip this week, and attributed the submissions to an automated testing process. "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable," they said. The July 18 tip purported to come from someone who might have information about the case, police added. "I may have information regarding this case," Anthropic's model wrote in its submission. "I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around (the street named on the page) during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant." The brackets featured in Anthropic's statement. Previous incidents have involved AI agents hacking into vulnerable systems or commandeering unsanctioned platforms to communicate with one another. In September, Anthropic rival OpenAI apologized for the hacking of an Australian health data portal by a rogue AI agent, the first known instance of an AI agent exploiting a government website. A BOGUS TIP In two cases described on Friday, Anthropic’s models obtained for free public data normally only available for a fee. Another instanced revealed an obscure flaw that allowed use of a public tool hosted by a university. Claude models were also able to bypass restrictions by using free services that shorten URLs. Philadelphia police said the tip "was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination." Knowingly giving false reports to law enforcement authorities is a misdemeanor under Pennsylvania law, which specifies "a person", however. This includes "information relating to an offense or incident when he knows he has no information relating to such offense or incident." Police quoted Anthropic as telling them the test process was stopped after discovery of the incident. The false tip was submitted through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com concerning an unsolved homicide. Police said they had no evidence of unauthorized access to their systems or compromise of their data.

item.title: Republican opposition widens to livestreamed execution; Trump still weighing it
item.description: Vice President JD Vance expressed skepticism over whether the Pentagon will proceed with livestreaming the execution.
item.dc:creator: Phil Stewart, Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: Republican US lawmakers joined religious leaders and international observers on Friday in opposing a Pentagon plan to livestream an execution by firing squad, while President Donald Trump said he has not yet decided whether to allow the live feed. Vice President JD Vance expressed skepticism over whether the Pentagon will proceed with livestreaming the scheduled December 3 execution of former US Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan, who was found guilty in a US military trial of fatally shooting 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. "I don't know that that's actually going to happen," Vance told reporters in Cincinnati, referring to the livestream plan championed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. If it is shown publicly, Vance said, "I'm not going to be watching it." Trump told reporters that Hasan deserves the death penalty by firing squad, calling him "totally nuts." But when asked if he wants the execution livestreamed, the Republican president said he has yet to "make a determination about that." A senior US Catholic bishop and a US evangelical Christian leader voiced opposition to the plan, as did the UN human rights office. REPUBLICANS VOICE CONCERN Several Republican US lawmakers argued against livestreaming. Senator John Curtis wrote on social media that "a civilization erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment." Senator Thom Tillis and Representative Austin Scott said livestreaming executions is what Islamist extremists would do. Representative Rob Bresnahan said the pain felt by victims and family members "deserves respect, not a public show." "This should be reconsidered," Representative Michael Baumgartner wrote on social media. Democrats were overwhelmingly opposed. The event would be extraordinary, even for a country that has long employed capital punishment. A government execution has never been broadcast or livestreamed, according to death penalty experts, and the US military has not executed anyone by firing squad since 1945. Hasan, now 56, is believed to be confined to a wheelchair, having been shot by police during his arrest. A senior White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Trump does not oppose the idea of livestreaming the execution but could change his mind. The White House is hearing concerns from lawmakers, allies and religious leaders who are urging the administration not to livestream it, the official said. Hegseth, a Trump appointee, confirmed the plans for the livestreamed execution on Thursday. 'A CULTURE OF DEATH' Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, condemned the planned livestream as a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death." Walter Kim, president of the National Association of Evangelicals, said on social media that a livestreamed execution by firing squad "risks turning one of the state's most solemn responsibilities into a public spectacle, promoting a culture of death, rather than a culture that upholds the dignity of every human being." Hegseth, a member of a conservative evangelical denomination, has made his Christian faith a hallmark of his tenure as defense secretary and has led prayer services at the Pentagon. He also has brushed off Pope Leo's criticism of the Iran war . Hasan, an American-born Muslim, said during his 2013 trial that he carried out the shootings to try to stop what he called a US war on Islam. "Whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people," Vance told reporters. 'FREE PROPAGANDA' Joe Kent, who resigned this year as Trump's head of the National Counterterrorism Center, wrote on social media: "Streaming his execution is not just a stain on our morality — it also gives the terrorists free propaganda that they will use to radicalize & recruit more terrorists." Brendan Carr, chair of the Federal Communications Commission, told CNBC it is his understanding that the execution would not air on broadcast TV but said he would [USN:L1N45V0M1 TEXT:"defer"] to Hegseth on whether US networks could air it. US law [USN:L1N45V0IV TEXT:"prohibits the recording or broadcasting"] of executions in the federal prison system. Military regulations have not applied that same prohibition. Courts have rejected lawsuits brought by media organizations seeking broader public access to executions. The UN human rights office said public executions violate prohibitions against torture. "Public executions constitute a form of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment," Shabia Mantoo, a spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, told a news briefing in Geneva. Amnesty International called the use of a firing squad "reprehensible." Mental health experts said it also could traumatize children. The execution is scheduled to be held at the same sprawling military base where Hasan opened fire with a handgun in a medical facility. The Pentagon on Friday declined to say whether families of those killed in Hasan's attack would be invited to attend the execution, as is common practice in US civilian executions. It remains unclear how the Army would select the shooters and what protocols might be followed during the execution itself. The Pentagon said it would release details later. The plan to livestream the execution comes at a time of heightened debate in the US over the death penalty following the [USN:L1N45M04O TEXT:"botched lethal injection"] last week of a Tennessee woman who was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder. The controversy has flared in the run-up to the November 3 US midterm elections in which Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress.

item.title: Fuerte terremoto sacude Panamá, sin registros de destrucción masiva
item.description: Un terremoto de magnitud 7.7 sacudió el sur de Panamá el viernes, causando daños en edificios y dejando a miles de personas asustadas en las calles, pero el país aparentemente evitó una destrucción generalizada o víctimas mortales.
item.dc:creator: Elida Moreno, Dave Sherwood
item.content:encoded: Un terremoto de magnitud 7.7 sacudió el sur de Panamá el viernes, causando daños en edificios y dejando a miles de personas asustadas en las calles, pero el país aparentemente evitó una destrucción generalizada o víctimas mortales. El Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS, por su sigla en inglés) informó que el epicentro se ubicó en una zona poco poblada a unos 200 kilómetros (km) de la capital y a una profundidad de 12.6 km. En las horas siguientes, a pesar de que decenas de réplicas sacudieron el istmo, el Canal de Panamá informó que operaba con normalidad y el Aeropuerto Internacional de Tocumen levantó la suspensión de vuelos. Los oficinistas del exclusivo centro de negocios de Ciudad de Panamá -una urbe de unas 410,000 personas- se preocupaban por cómo regresar a casa en medio del caos vehicular, después de que el terremoto empujo a miles a las calles en busca de resguardo. Juan Sánchez, un empleado del Ministerio de Economía de 37 años, esperaba un autobús que, según dijo, dudaba que llegara. "Evacuaron todos estos edificios. Todos están afuera. Ahora el problema es, ¿cómo volvemos a casa?", se preguntó. El presidente Raúl Mulino viajó a Penonomé, una ciudad ubicada a medio camino entre el epicentro y Ciudad de Panamá, donde algunos edificios se derrumbaron y una iglesia resultó dañada. A pesar de la fuerza del movimiento telúrico del viernes, el país parece haberse librado de la destrucción causada por otros sismos recientes y potentes en la región. Por el momento, no se reportaron muertos ni heridos. En junio, [USN:L6N42Y0SA TEXT:"dos potentes sismos"] consecutivos en Venezuela causaron la muerte de más de 6,500 personas, mientras que un terremoto en [USN:L1N4480IR TEXT:"Colombia"] en agosto dejó más de 300 fallecidos. Un informe del USGS estimó que alrededor de 43,000 panameños vivían en áreas con al menos una exposición severa al terremoto. Esto se compara con casi 1.4 millones en el área de los dos sismos en Venezuela y más de 1.6 millones en la zona afectada por el terremoto en el oeste de Colombia. VIBRACIONES PROLONGADAS Néstor Luque, director del Instituto de Geociencias de Panamá, atribuyó el sismo al sistema de fallas Azuero-Soná que, según explicó, contiene una enorme acumulación de presión que se libera ocasionalmente. "Las señales sísmicas se propagaron por todo el territorio nacional, por eso se sintió en todas partes", dijo. En Ciudad de Panamá, Luque dijo haber contado 40 segundos de vibraciones, aunque en otras zonas es posible que se hayan sentido temblores aún más prolongados. Sabina Ríos, quien se encontraba en el sexto piso de un antiguo edificio militar estadounidense en Ciudad de Panamá, dijo que el temblor fue inusualmente fuerte y prolongado. "El sismo se sintió fuerte y duró mucho tiempo, el más largo que he sentido en años", dijo Ríos. Víctor Pinzón, un trabajador de mantenimiento de 48 años, dijo a Reuters que había visto a los limpiadores de ventanas de rascacielos soportar el temblor. "Es un milagro que no hayan muerto", dijo. "Parecía que estaban meciéndose en una hamaca", agregó. Los terremotos fuertes no son comunes en Panamá, y algunos ancianos lloraban mientras evacuaban a las calles. "Estamos asustados, solos los dos aquí, la casa se nos rajó y tememos que se nos caiga encima", dijo Ricardo Brown, de 74 años, en una conversación telefónica desde la zona Las Minas, en la provincia de Herrera, al sur de Panamá, donde el sismo dañó varias viviendas. Omar Smith, director de la agencia de protección civil de Panamá, declaró al medio Telemetro que también se habían reportado impactos en Chitré, la capital de Herrera, y en la costa de la provincia de Los Santos.

item.title: Forte terremoto atinge Panamá, mas não causa grandes destruições
item.description: Um terremoto de magnitude 7,7 atingiu o sul do Panamá nesta sexta-feira, causando danos a edifícios e levando milhares de pessoas às ruas, mas o país parece ter escapado de uma destruição generalizada ou de vítimas fatais.
item.dc:creator: Elida Moreno, Dave Sherwood
item.content:encoded: Um terremoto de magnitude 7,7 atingiu o sul do Panamá nesta sexta-feira, causando danos a edifícios e levando milhares de pessoas às ruas, mas o país parece ter escapado de uma destruição generalizada ou de vítimas fatais. O Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos informou que o terremoto ocorreu a uma profundidade de 12,6 km, com epicentro em uma área pouco povoada a cerca de 200 km da capital, e que havia possibilidade de algumas vítimas. Nas horas seguintes, mesmo com mais de 40 réplicas abalando o país do istmo, o Canal do Panamá e a mina de cobre Cobre Panamá informaram que as operações estavam normais, e o Aeroporto Internacional de Tocumen revogou a suspensão dos voos. Funcionários de escritórios no sofisticado centro financeiro do centro da Cidade do Panamá se preocupavam em como chegar em casa no meio do engarrafamento, depois que o terremoto levou milhares de pessoas às ruas. Juan Sánchez, um funcionário de 37 anos do Ministério da Economia, esperava por um ônibus que, segundo ele, duvidava que chegaria. “Eles evacuaram todos esses prédios. Todo mundo está na rua. Agora o problema é: como vamos chegar em casa?” O presidente Raúl Mulino viajou para Penonomé, uma cidade localizada a meio caminho entre o epicentro e a Cidade do Panamá, onde alguns prédios desabaram e uma igreja foi danificada. Apesar da intensidade do tremor desta sexta-feira, o país parece ter sido poupado da destruição causada por outros fortes terremotos recentes na região, sem que tenham sido relatadas mortes ou feridos imediatamente. Tremores consecutivos na Venezuela, em junho, mataram vários milhares de pessoas, enquanto um terremoto na Colômbia, em agosto, matou mais de 300. Um relatório de exposição elaborado pelo USGS estimou que cerca de 43 mil panamenhos viviam em áreas com exposição pelo menos grave ao terremoto. Isso se compara a quase 1,4 milhão na área dos terremotos gêmeos na Venezuela e a mais de 1,6 milhão na zona atingida pelo terremoto no oeste da Colômbia. VIBRAÇÕES PROLONGADAS Nestor Luque, diretor do instituto de geociências do Panamá, disse que o terremoto foi desencadeado pelo Sistema de Falhas de Azuero-Sona, que há muito tempo acumulava pressão. “É um sistema de falhas ativas que, ocasionalmente, devido ao acúmulo de tensão, libera essa quantidade de energia”, disse ele. “Os sinais sísmicos se propagaram por todo o território nacional e é por isso que puderam ser sentidos em todos os lugares.” Na Cidade do Panamá, Luque disse ter contado 40 segundos de vibrações, embora outras áreas possam ter sentido tremores ainda mais longos. Sabina Ríos, que estava no sexto andar de um antigo prédio da época da ocupação militar dos EUA na Cidade do Panamá, disse que o tremor foi excepcionalmente forte e prolongado. “O terremoto foi forte e durou muito tempo, o mais longo que senti em anos”, disse Ríos. Víctor Pinzón, um funcionário de manutenção de 48 anos, contou à Reuters que viu limpadores de janelas de arranha-céus resistindo ao tremor. “É um milagre que eles não tenham morrido”, disse ele. “Parecia que estavam balançando em uma rede.” Terremotos fortes não são comuns no Panamá, e alguns moradores idosos choravam enquanto evacuavam para as ruas. “Estamos com medo. Somos só nós dois, idosos, aqui. A casa rachou e temos medo de que ela desabe sobre nós”, disse Ricardo Brown, de 74 anos, na província de Herrera, no sul do Panamá, onde afirmou ter visto várias casas danificadas. Omar Smith, que chefia a agência de proteção civil do Panamá, disse ao veículo de notícias Telemetro Reporta que também foram relatados tremores em Chitre, capital de Herrera, e ao longo da costa na província de Los Santos. O USGS estimou que as perdas econômicas poderiam chegar de 1% a 10% do Produto Interno Bruto do Panamá, e a concessionária de energia Naturgy relatou cortes de energia em seis províncias. O Panamá tinha programado um exercício nacional de retirada para a segunda-feira da próxima semana, a fim de testar as capacidades de resposta a emergências do país em caso de terremotos.

item.title: Trump selects Katie Zacharia as White House press secretary
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he has appointed Katie Zacharia, a communications adviser for his Truth Social platform, to serve as White House press secretary following Karoline Leavitt's departure in August.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he has appointed Katie Zacharia, a communications adviser for his Truth Social platform, to serve as White House press secretary following Karoline Leavitt's [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"departure"] in August. He said Zacharia has an "unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter." "I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The New York Times first reported the news of her appointment. The selection will put Zacharia at the center of the White House's public messaging operation in the final stretch before next month's midterm elections , when Trump's agenda and his party's control of Congress will be put before voters. Zacharia said in a social media post that she welcomed the appointment and looks forward to "working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country" to get Trump's message out. Trump's approval rating fell to 32% — the lowest of his political career — as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living and the Iran war , a recent [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos"] poll found. The selection of Zacharia underscores the close ties between Trump's administration and his broader political and media operation. It comes after Trump Media unveiled in July that for a fee it would give banks and trading firms "the fastest" [USN:L4N43I1AE TEXT:"access to posts"] from influential Truth Social accounts, such as the president's, whose posts often move global markets. Zacharia has worked as a senior communications adviser for Truth Social, the Republican president's social media platform, and the Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT.O) since June, according to her LinkedIn page. She briefly served as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security before departing in March. Zacharia, an attorney who frequently appears on conservative outlets Fox News and Newsmax, previously worked as a legal adviser for Fix California, a conservative group that aims to address what it described as "the left's stranglehold" on state politics. The group was founded by Richard Grenell, who has served as Trump's envoy to Venezuela and the interim president and executive director of the Kennedy Center in Washington. Zacharia interned at the White House during President George W. Bush's administration.

item.title: Strong Panama quake shakes nation, but avoids major destruction
item.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and sending thousands into the streets, but the country appeared to escape widespread destruction or deaths.
item.dc:creator: Elida Moreno, Dave Sherwood
item.content:encoded: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and sending thousands into the streets, but the country appeared to escape widespread destruction or deaths. The US Geological Survey said the earthquake hit at a depth of 12.6 km (7.8 miles), with an epicenter in a sparsely populated area about 200 km (124 miles) from the capital, and that some casualties were possible. In the following hours, even as more than 40 aftershocks rattled the isthmus nation, the Panama Canal and Cobre Panama copper mine reported normal operations and the Tocumen International Airport lifted a suspension on flights. Office workers in the upscale business hub of downtown Panama City fretted about how to get home in the snarl of traffic, after the quake sent thousands into the streets. Juan Sanchez, a 37-year-old economy ministry employee, waited for a bus he said he doubted would arrive. "They evacuated all of these buildings. Everyone is outside. Now the problem is, how do we get home?" President Raul Mulino traveled to Penonome, a city about halfway between the epicenter and Panama City, where some buildings collapsed and a church was damaged. Despite the force of Friday's tremor, the country appeared to have been spared the [USN:L6N44903E TEXT:"destruction"] of other recent powerful quakes in the [USN:L6N42X19G TEXT:"region"], with no deaths or injuries immediately reported. Back-to-back quakes in Venezuela in June killed several thousand people, while a quake in Colombia in August killed more than 300. An exposure report by the USGS estimated about 43,000 Panamanians lived in areas with at least severe exposure to the quake. This compares to nearly 1.4 million in the area of the twin quakes in Venezuela and over 1.6 million in the quake-hit zone of western Colombia. PROLONGED VIBRATIONS Nestor Luque, director of Panama's geosciences institute, attributed the quake to the Azuero Sona Fault System that he said contained a massive buildup of pressure that is occasionally released. "The seismic signals have traveled throughout the national territory and that is why it could be felt everywhere." In Panama City, Luque said he counted 40 seconds of vibrations, though other areas may have felt even longer tremors. Sabina Rios, who was on the sixth floor of an old US military-era building in Panama City, said the shaking was unusually strong and prolonged. "The quake felt strong and lasted a long time, the longest I’ve felt in years,” Rios said. Victor Pinzon, a 48-year-old maintenance worker, told Reuters he had watched high-rise window cleaners ride out the shaking. “It’s a miracle they didn’t get killed,” he said. “They looked like they were swinging in a hammock.” Strong earthquakes are not common in Panama, and some elderly residents were in tears as they evacuated into the streets. “We’re scared. It’s just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked, and we’re afraid it could fall on us,” said Ricardo Brown, 74, in Herrera province in southern Panama, where he said he saw a number of damaged homes. Omar Smith, who heads Panama's civil protection agency, told news outlet Telemetro Reporta that impacts had also been reported in Chitre, the capital of Herrera, and along the coast in Los Santos province. The USGS estimated economic losses could amount to 1% to 10% of Panama's gross domestic product, and electricity provider Naturgy reported power outages in six provinces. Panama was due to hold a national evacuation drill on Monday of next week to test the country's emergency response.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro descarta privatização da Petrobras como "boataria"
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, negou nesta sexta-feira rumores de que, se for eleito, tentará privatizar a Petrobras e outras empresas estatais.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, negou nesta sexta-feira rumores de que, se for eleito, tentará privatizar a Petrobras (PETR3.SA) e outras empresas estatais. Segundo ele, existe uma onda de boatos contra a sua candidatura para tentar reverter a liderança que teve no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial. “Isso é uma boataria, é uma boataria atrás da outra”, disse Flávio a jornalistas na entrada de um encontro com apoiadores e empresários na zona sudoeste do Rio de Janeiro. Flávio Bolsonaro venceu o primeiro turno da eleição presidencial com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição. As primeiras pesquisas após a votação de domingo mostram que o senador continua à frente do petista antes do segundo turno, marcado para o dia 25 deste mês. Ao ser questionado se pretendia mudar o comando da estatal, caso seja eleito, o candidato do PL disse que primeiro é preciso mudar o presidente da República. Durante o governo de seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, vários ativos e bens da empresa, como refinarias, foram vendidos, num movimento visto por alguns como uma tentativa de esvaziar e enfraquecer a companhia para viabilizar uma futura venda. Flávio Bolsonaro acusou ainda o atual governo de estar preparando uma bomba para os consumidores brasileiros com programas de subsídio, subvenção e desoneração de combustíveis. Nesta sexta-feira, o [USN:L1N45V0MB TEXT:"governo anunciou"] a ampliação dessas medidas para diesel, gasolina e etanol por 30 dias. O governo alega que essas iniciativas são necessárias para minimizar os impactos da guerra no Oriente Médio que afeta petróleo e derivados. "O atual governo, muita gente não percebeu ainda, qual é a outra bomba que ele vai jogar no consumidor, quem usa moto, carros e caminhoneiros. O Lula pela Petrobras deu um subsídio de 2 reais no preço do diesel. Ele acaba no dia seguinte à eleição. É isso que esse governo irresponsável está fazendo“, disse Flávio. Em entrevista coletiva em Brasília para anunciar a prorrogação, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, negou que ela tenha relação com o período eleitoral e disse que os preços internacionais do petróleo seguem pressionados por causa da guerra no Oriente Médio. No início da tarde desta sexta, os preços do petróleo Brent LCOc1 operavam próximos a US$104, muito acima dos níveis ao redor de US$70 observados antes do início da guerra.

item.title: Holland & Knight, other firms disclose data security breaches
item.description: Two more large US law firms, Holland & Knight and Squire Patton Boggs, have disclosed data security breaches to state regulators, and a third was hit with a new proposed class action in federal court over a reported hack.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Two more large US law firms, Holland & Knight and Squire Patton Boggs, have disclosed data security breaches to state regulators, and a third was hit with a new proposed class action in federal court over a reported hack. Holland & Knight, which employs 2,200 lawyers, and the 2,600-attorney Squire Patton Boggs both told Vermont’s state attorney general on Thursday that Social Security numbers were exposed in the incidents that affected the firms. Holland & Knight in a statement said "a threat actor used social engineering techniques to gain unauthorized remote access to a firm computer." It said it "identified the small number of files involved and promptly notified the clients whose information was contained in those files." Squire Patton Boggs in a statement said its incident involved "an unauthorized third party obtaining a limited set of information from the firm." Both firms said there was no disruption to their client services. Separately, law firm Nelson Mullins was sued on Wednesday in federal court in South Carolina for allegedly failing to safeguard private information following a breach at the firm. In a statement, the firm said a cyber group that targets law firms “accessed the laptop of a single user and copied a limited number of documents accessible by this user.” The firm, which employs more than 1,000 lawyers, said the incident “was contained and did not involve any other systems, devices, or accounts.” Nelson Mullins said it was in contact with law enforcement authorities and supporting their investigation. The latest disclosures underscore cybersecurity risks for law firms, which routinely hold sensitive client communications, financial records and personal data that can be valuable to hackers. Recent breaches at major law firms have highlighted how cybercriminals are increasingly targeting the legal industry through tactics including so-called social-engineering schemes designed to gain access to confidential information. Several law firms including WilmerHale and Weil Gotshal have paid a ransom or suppression payment following a data breach. WilmerHale is also facing a lawsuit in DC federal court over its alleged breach.
